title: Nine Dead After Devastating Murder-Suicide at Pennsylvania Home, Police Say
snippet: A horrific murder-suicide in Erie, Pennsylvania, left nine people dead, including two young children and a pregnant woman, authorities reported Saturday.
content:
ERIE, Pa. — A quiet northwestern Pennsylvania community was left in shock after a 45-year-old man killed eight people—including two young children and a pregnant woman—before taking his own life inside an Erie home, local authorities said Saturday.

Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah confirmed that the gunman was related to seven of the victims. The eighth victim was a friend of the pregnant woman.

A Horrific Sequence of Events

According to audio and video evidence gathered by investigators, muffled gunshot sounds were recorded coming from inside the residence shortly before 5 p.m. Friday. Moments later, two distressed women arrived at the property and frantically pounded on the front door. The shooter emerged and opened fire on the women as they ran toward him, leaving both dead outside the home.

Law enforcement arrived within minutes following an alert from ShotSpotter, an automated gunshot detection system. Upon finding the two deceased women outside, officers deployed a drone and a robotic device to assess the interior before entering.

Inside, tactical teams uncovered a scene of immense devastation: a 5-year-old boy and a 1-year-old girl were found dead on the first floor; two additional women and two young men were located in a stairwell; and the gunman was found dead on the second floor from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

"Out of respect for the victims and the families, I will not discuss the details of what our officers encountered inside that home," Chief Lorah stated during a news conference. "But I want our community to understand the gravity of what happened and the profound impact this tragedy has had on those involved and on our community as a whole."

Investigators Search for Motive

While police have not released a motive, Chief Lorah indicated that detectives will examine cellphones and interview surviving relatives, noting that the two women who arrived at the house appeared to know trouble was brewing. "They knew something was going on at that house," Lorah said. "We have to figure out what that is."

Lorah also clarified that loud noises heard by neighbors during the police response were flashbang devices deployed by SWAT officers, not additional gunfire.

Community and State Officials Mourn

The tragedy in Erie, situated roughly 120 miles north of Pittsburgh, prompted outpouring support from local and state leaders. Erie Mayor Daria Devlin addressed the grieving families directly during Saturday's briefing, offering her deepest condolences and promising the city's full support.

District Attorney Elizabeth Hirz urged the public to refrain from spreading unverified rumors while the investigation remains active, asking the community to respect the grieving families.

Speaking at an event near Philadelphia, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro offered state assistance and reflected on the tragedy alongside a separate early-morning shooting of two Philadelphia police officers. "Today has been a dark day across this commonwealth," Shapiro said.
